headline: Bangladesh mission thought executed citizens faced prison not death, in KSA
summary: Officials at Bangladesh's Jeddah mission believed two citizens executed in Saudi Arabia were serving prison terms, not the death penalty, the foreign ministry informed a parliamentary committee. This misunderstanding stemmed from how prisoners were categorized
details: Officials at Bangladesh’s mission in Jeddah believed that two Bangladeshis executed in Saudi Arabia faced prison terms ranging from six months to 15 years, rather than the death penalty. The foreign ministry conveyed this information to a parliamentary committee yesterday.

The ministry explained that the categorization of prisoners on a list from Saudi Arabia had led officials to this belief. They have since sought answers from the Saudi authorities regarding the incident.

The parliamentary committee has asked the ministry to provide a full report once Saudi Arabia responds. They also requested an inquiry into potential negligence at the Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah and measures to prevent future occurrences.

The two Bangladeshi nationals were executed in Saudi Arabia on October 14 without prior notification to Dhaka. They had been detained since August 2023 over separate allegations, one involving “cybercrime” and the other “adultery.”

Saudi Arabia had sent a list of approximately 2,500 prisoners about 14 days before the executions, which included the names of the two Bangladeshis. However, their cases were not properly identified on this list.

A foreign ministry official, speaking anonymously, noted that Saudi Arabia can impose the death penalty for certain cybercrimes, though it's not universal. Death sentences for adultery are extremely rare, with prison terms being more common.

The official added that it was difficult to discern the death sentences from the conviction details, especially since the sentence column was left blank in the shared lists. This contributed to the mission's misunderstanding.

The parliamentary committee also addressed reports of abuse faced by Bangladeshi women workers in Saudi Arabia and other Middle Eastern countries. The foreign ministry reported that around one to two percent of the 169,000 Bangladeshi women workers in Saudi Arabia experience abuse.

The ministry informed the committee that 1,364 women domestic workers had been rescued and safely repatriated. The committee urged the ministry to implement necessary measures to eliminate such incidents entirely.

Committee chairman Zohra Adib Chowdhury highlighted weaknesses in the overall process, questioning why the consulate had not acted earlier despite good relations with Saudi Arabia. She emphasized the need for better examination of reports.

headline: Two DGFI members among 6 arrested over alleged kidnapping and extortion in Dhaka
summary: The suspects allegedly held a businessman captive in Mohammadpur, demanding Tk 100,000 in ransom. They were detained after the victim escaped and sought police help.
details: Six people, including two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) and a Bangladesh Ansar member, have been arrested over the alleged kidnapping and extortion of a businessman in Dhaka. The suspects are accused of holding him captive in Mohammadpur and demanding Tk 100,000 in ransom.

The arrests occurred in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar on Saturday night after the businessman escaped and sought help from police near Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute. The suspects were later handed over to Mohammadpur Police Station and subsequently sent to jail by a Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate.

The arrestees include DGFI headquarters Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Nuruzzaman, Ansar member Sohel Rana, private company security guard Mukul Gazi, Mahfuzur Rahman, and Ziaul Islam. Two other individuals, Sonia and Fonirul (also known as Monirul), have also been accused in the case.

Md Sharif, a motorcycle dealer from Shyamoli, filed the case, alleging he was lured to a house in Chandrima Model Town on Saturday under the pretext of buying a motorcycle. According to the first information report, Sharif knew Sohel as they lived in neighboring houses, and Sohel took him to the house where a woman named Sonia was introduced as Sohel’s sister.

After Sohel left the room, the other suspects allegedly arrived, assaulted Sharif, and demanded Tk 100,000. Sharif stated he paid Tk 70,000 but was beaten again because the group was unhappy with the amount, and he was kept captive while trying to arrange the remaining money.

Around 3 AM, the suspects took Sharif out of the house and put him in a Toyota vehicle parked opposite the Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar. When the suspects stepped out to have tea, Sharif spotted a police patrol vehicle and sought help, leading officers to intervene and arrest the six.

Police officials, speaking anonymously, noted that the arrests became complicated after two of the suspects were identified as DGFI members. Officials from Army Headquarters later visited the police station to verify their identities before the suspects were formally arrested and produced before the court.
